utterances.text: Did you ever review the discussion, because the minutes also have rather interesting presentations by the various folks that were there, giving their interpretations and giving their opinions with respect to the questions. Did you ever review that as either president or outgoing president of HDZ or someone who was interested in what was -- you know, in this particular discussion?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. If we could just look at -- and thank you very much for that answer. If we could look at 117. I don't know if -- let's see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel Karnavas, we're going to have to stop at 5.00 because the Judges have asked for that. We'll have 15 minutes more tomorrow morning. So instead of finishing at 5.15 tomorrow, we'll be finishing at 5.30, but please see if you can finish by 5.00 today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you for the warning for tomorrow, Your Honour. Well, this discussion is going to take a little bit more than five minutes. We can try to just touch on it, because I don't like to waste any time, so -- but thank you very much. I will just -- I'll try to be pithy in my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you see that document, sir? You see the two questions that are on page 2 of this particular document? It's 00117.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can see is the Livno question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. If you go down the page, if you scroll down the page and if it's not possible, perhaps we can give you a Croat version.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it now, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to read them separately, separately just so -- and then we can kind of deconstruct them, if you will, and I know that you're not a jurist. The one -- the first one, that is the one that's being proposed at Livno, says, "Are you in favour of a sovereign and independent Bosnia-Herzegovina, a joint state of the constitutive and sovereign Croatian, Muslim, and Serbian people in their ethnic areas," and in parentheses "as cantons?" with a question mark. Now, if we go to the one that was passed by the Assembly that ultimately, as I understand it, people voted on. This one says: "Are you in favour of a sovereign and independent Bosnia-Herzegovina, a state of equal citizens -- equal citizens and peoples Croats, Muslims, Serbs, and other peoples who live in it?" Now, if we just look at them side by side, we can see what exactly the Croats in Livno are trying to inject into the question. Do you see it, sir?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. First of all, I have to tell you that everything that was done in Livno was done belatedly and was no longer valid. It couldn't be implemented. That's the first thing you should realise. Secondly, in Livno, national cantons were called for, and at that time that was contrary to the constitution, because there were no national cantons since our Commission for Cantonisation never reached agreement. Let me ask you, what are national cantons? So there weren't any. Now, in the official version, there's a very important point which relates to citizens and nations. So in Bosnia and Herzegovina, as opposed to countries like your own, you didn't always have the sovereignty of citizens.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You didn't always only have the sovereignty of citizens, because it was contrary to our system, one vote, one citizen. There was the protection of national interests which today in Bosnia-Herzegovina ended with the Chamber of Nations or House of Nations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And that was -- but let me just back up a little bit. And I just -- I just want to cover what's in the questions, okay? So if we could go step-by-step. It would appear that what is being proposed, whether it's belated or not, that's a separate topic. We'll cover that, because as I understand it, the Croats within the HDZ held you personally responsible for not promoting this question and not getting it on the table and not pushing it, and that was one of the reasons why they wanted you out of the party as their president. But that's a separate issue. We can cover that tomorrow. For today, the two minutes that we have left, it would appear that the question that is being promoted at Livno has the word in it "sovereignty" for a reason. It talks about a joint state of the constitutive and sovereign Croatian, Muslim, and Serbian peoples. Now, that was more or less guaranteed within the 1974 constitution, was it not? What they're asking, is it not --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have to show me that. Show me our version. I can't see it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. It's up -- it's at the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still can't see it. All right. Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. "Are you in favour of a sovereign and independent Bosnia-Herzegovina --" I think we all agree that everybody was -- all right, "a joint state -- a joint state --" meaning a joint state of three nations, three nations within the geographical region -- "of the constitutive and sovereign Croatian, Muslim, and Serbian peoples in their ethnic areas." What they're asking, sir, is it not what was guaranteed to them in the 1974 constitution? They're just looking for a little protection, recognising that they are a nation, one of three in this geographical region of which they're going to have to share the space; right?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Croatian nation was recognised by the constitution of 1974, and previous ones as well, and it was impossible to make a state community. You must know what a state community is. It's not a state. It's not the same thing as a state.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's not -- that's not the essence of my question. It has nothing to do with the state community. I'm asking you, because I have 10 seconds left, does this question not take into consideration what was guaranteed in 19 -- in the 1974 constitution? What they're asking for is a joint state, joint state - not separate; joint - of the constitutive and sovereign Croatian, Muslim, and Serbian peoples, which were recognised by the constitution of 1974. Isn't that what they're asking? It's a yes or a no, because then we're going to have to break for the day.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they can ask whatever they want but that has no foundation in the constitution. There are no elements for a state community and there are no elements for national cantons either. Now, the fact that they're asking for this --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir. Sir. You're an intelligent human being. You understand English, and you certainly understand the wonderful translation that you're getting. You know and I know that's not the form of my question. Now, the form of my question is isn't what they're asking? I'm not talking about the cantons that's in parentheses. What they're asking here, are they not saying they want to be in a joint state of the constitutive and sovereign Croatian, Muslim, and Serbian peoples? It's a joint state, not a separate state. They're not asking for partition. Isn't that the essence of this question? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, just a moment. Either the translation is not the right one or you can't understand the nuances, the shades of meaning. The state community is something that was Serbia and Montenegro until yesterday. Now, to look for this -- look for a state community within Bosnia-Herzegovina is to ask and look for the impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're going to have to pick up on this, and I don't believe I mentioned anything about a state community, but just for the record, I've asked the question three times and this may take a little bit longer to cross-examine the gentleman as a result of the non-responsive answers that I'm getting. Thank you very much, and I apologise for going over I believe two minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you. We reconvene tomorrow morning at 9.00. And as I said a moment ago, instead of finishing at 5.15, we're going to go on working until 5.30. Thank you one and all, and a very good evening to you.
